summary: AgroShift helps farmers and local advisors turn raw NASA climate data into practical crop-rotation plans. By typing in a farm's coordinates, current crop, soil type, and main goal :- whether saving water, rebuilding soil nitrogen, or handling extreme heat, users can compare sticking with their current crop against two climate-smart alternatives backed by live NASA POWER weather data, SMAP soil moisture trends, and ECOSTRESS heat benchmarks.
details:
Why We Built This Planting the exact same crop season after season wears down the soil. When dry spells hit or post-harvest fields sit bare under intense sun, moisture evaporates fast, pests build up, and farmers end up spending more on water and synthetic fertilizer just to keep yields steady. Satellite datasets can warn us about these shifts early, but raw climate tables aren't helpful to someone standing in a field trying to decide what to sow next.

How AgroShift Works We built AgroShift as a fast, no-install web app that works right on a phone or tablet browser:

1. Live Local Climate Check: You enter a farm's latitude and longitude, pick your current crop (Maize, Winter Wheat, Cotton, or Paddy Rice), choose your soil texture (Loam, Sandy, or Clay), and set your top priority. AgroShift pulls live seasonal peak temperatures (T2M_MAX) and rainfall totals (PRECTOTCORR) directly from the NASA POWER API. 2. Spotting Soil & Heat Stress: It pairs those live climate numbers with SMAP root-zone moisture benchmarks and ECOSTRESS thermal stress windows to pinpoint when your field is most likely to dry out or overheat between harvests. 3. Comparing Your Options Side by Side: Instead of giving a single rigid command, AgroShift lays out three clear paths: - Baseline: What happens if you keep planting the same monoculture. - Climate-Resilient Shift: Rotating into hardier crops like sorghum, pearl millet, or chickpea during hot, dry stretches. - Soil & Nitrogen Builder: Adding legumes and cover crops to shield bare soil from the sun and naturally fix 40–80 kg of nitrogen per hectare. 4. Honest Caveats Built In: Satellite pixels cover wide areas and can't see everything happening in one specific acre. Every card clearly flags what needs a local check first: like testing exact soil pH, checking local seed supply, or timing cover-crop termination. Real-World Impact Because AgroShift is lightweight and includes an offline fallback mode, it loads quickly even on spotty rural mobile networks. It gives growers a straightforward way to cut irrigation pressure by 25–35%, rely less on chemical fertilizers, and keep their soil covered year-round.
